scope: Primary-document strategy research and static archived source inspection only. No project/source/host edits, compilation, tests, transactions, or live-provider qualification. Dedicated external research files only.
question: How do CL managers bound residual positions, handle one-sided inventory/reversal, and limit costs/manipulation?

sources.version_limit: Guide says last update August2024; do not assume its six-hour cadence or harvest behavior is every current deployment.

sources.qualification: Whole Beefy, NOT CLM-only TVL; no comparable ALM rank claimed.

protocols.architecture: Main plus one alternative position; rebalance redeploys paired inventory first and assigns the residual asset to the alt. The protocol describes avoiding token-sale rebalances, not eliminating inventory risk.
protocols.risks: The alt may dominate the portfolio during a persistent trend. Mark-to-market divergence versus holding remains; not swapping does not undo economic losses. The2026 Ethereum article describes private RPCs, improved on-chain harvest/reset controls and performance analysis; these are mitigations, not manipulation immunity.

Static details below; do not copy old permissive bounds/minima or combine harvest behavior with PoPL hourly harvesting.

sources.qualification: Cached snapshots differ across DefiLlama pages; treat as approximate context, not a shared atomic snapshot.

protocols.architecture: The engine accepts target tick/weight arrays for multiple positions. A strategy may use limit positions with skipSwap=true; Classic Rebalance explicitly also supports buying/selling. Thus neither a universal two-position cap nor universally swapless behavior follows from the protocol name.
protocols.relevance: Its documented percentage-of-range trigger is close to the proposed85% trigger. Its one-way exit option and separate trigger choices show that range semantics are strategy policy, not mandatory full exit. Execution price limits constrain swaps; adverse selection and market-path risk remain.
protocols.unknown: Did not independently inspect current deployed Steer tend implementation or prove a universal old-position replacement policy. No claim that Steer permits uncontrolled accumulated residual legs.

protocols.architecture: Inventory-oriented, with a preferred deposit asset. Healthy inventory can remain unchanged; over/under-inventory may require selling/buying, and high volatility can broaden ranges. Documentation says repositioning often avoids swaps, not that every adjustment is swapless.
protocols.relevance: Use explicit inventory policy and avoid reacting to every small price move; a passive range alone does not force portfolio balance. Published high-level documents do not establish one exact universal position-count cap or algorithm for every present vault.
protocols.limits: No exact current ICHI source deployment/range cap independently pinned here; do not infer all current vaults use two legs or literal controllerless operations from broad marketing.

protocols.architecture: Withdraws a managed NFT position and recreates a range of the same width around current price. Bots source swaps via0x subject to a configured price-impact limit, and contract checks compare to the pool TWAP. Residual tokens return to the position owner.
protocols.relevance: Replaces one managed leg instead of accumulating residual legs. Using swaps provides an immediate ratio at execution cost and MEV exposure; limits/TWAP restrict rather than eliminate risk. Its residual payout policy is incompatible with PoPL permanent principal and must not be copied.

function_findings.finding: Attempts main using paired budget; _checkAmounts299 requires positive amounts of both assets. Then recomputes remaining balances and mints at the single alt range. Does not perform a principal balancing swap.
Gets both existing keys, burns their complete liquidity and collects before bounds change. Old liquidity is not left behind when setting the next pair.
Claims fees, removes both legs, selects new ticks and redeploys. Guarded by onlyCalmPeriods and onlyRebalancers. Control privilege alone cannot prevent external price manipulation.

LetF=floor(currentTick/spacing)*spacing, W=positionWidth*spacing. Main[F−W,F+W]. Excess token0 alt[F+spacing,F+W]; excess token1 alt[F−W,F−spacing]. The alt stays inside main bounds with one-spacing separation from current tick; it is not anchored to the previous centre.
Collects/removes both and re-adds at retained ticks; does not call_setTicks. This behavior must not be imported into PoPL independent no-swap hourly fee harvesting.
Bounds spot tick relative to a configured same-pool TWAP; quality depends on real history depth/settings. Not an independent-price guarantee.

Archived width setter has no explicit minimum-width check. Positive alt width mathematically requiresW>spacing. Equality of balance values takes neither alt-selection branch and can retain previous alt bounds. These are reasons to adopt the architecture rather than blindly copy this old implementation.

derived_scenarios.case: Both legs end as the same asset
derived_scenarios.deduction: After withdrawing only one asset remains; main fails the two-positive-amount check, while the alt can hold that asset one-sided. No automatic forced swap or guarantee of an immediately fee-earning balanced main is present in this path.

Re-entry can trade the passive leg back unless liquidity is removed. At a subsequent adjustment both legs are combined first, then inventory/ranges recomputed; there is no append-only third/fourth alt.

Passive placement cannot manufacture the scarce asset. Waiting/retargeting a one-sided position preserves directional inventory exposure and may leave capital outside current trading, whereas forced conversion pays known trading fees/impact/MEV risk.

popl_design_inferences_not_implemented: Use a bounded1main+1secondary representation, consolidate before replacement, and include both in shares/NAV/fees/exit/canonical operations.

Do not equate a one-sided range with instant balancing or guaranteed fees. If both legs contain only one asset, select explicit wait/retarget/guarded-swap policy rather than pretend another active balanced LP can be minted.
Passive no-swap placement avoids one exposed active balancing swap, but passive trades still face adverse selection and reversible conversion; fees may not compensate inventory loss.
Do not copy Beefy deposit/harvest behavior into PoPL: entrants remain isolated and hourly harvesting remains distinct.

A meaningful strategy comparison must track net NAV versus holding, in-range share/time, inventory concentration, all execution costs and swap/position churn across trend, reversal, oscillation and no-counterliquidity paths.
research_gaps: Current live source/runtime/version pins for every third-party product are not verified; archived Beefy source is explicitly historical.
No protocol doc supplies a universal IL/MEV-free solution; high TVL is scale context, not proof of a suitable or safe strategy.
Actual funding, secondary lifecycle, cooldown and same-asset behavior remain user/design decisions; this research does not silently settle them.
